question: Section 8 says attribution 'ranks the parts the wrong way round'. Across the eight groups the trees' attribution ranks agree positively with the add-alone gains (Spearman +0.5 to +0.7 every bar, +0.8 to +0.9 ordinary days); it is reversed only for FOMC vs the realized moments. Narrow the sentence to that pair?

Retitle 'Attribution understates the FOMC calendar' and correct the realized-moments clause (largest exogenous group, second-largest removal).

final_answer: Yes, narrow it, to the trees' FOMC calendar rather than to the pair: the calendar is out of order against the realized moments, liquidity and both constituent groups, and the realized moments are the second-largest removal, so the 'converse' clause goes. Two edits in writeup/rehaul/08_feature_importance.tex, old text kept verbatim in dated % comments ('% 2026-10-29 (Q-2026-10-29-26, inferred T2). Was: ...'). (1) Replace the bullet at lines 349-358 with: \item \textbf{The trees' attribution understates the FOMC calendar.} The trees attribute \rhfipHarMin--\rhfipHarMax\% of their forecasts to the HAR terms, \rhfipMomMin--\rhfipMomMax\% to the futures' realized moments and \rhfipFomcBucketMin--\rhfipFomcBucketMax\% to the FOMC calendar (Appendix~\ref{app:rh_fi_rank}). Yet the calendar carries most of their accuracy gain. Added alone to the HAR benchmark set it changes QLIKE by \rhabLgbmAddFomcAllPct, \rhabXgbAddFomcAllPct{} and \rhabRfAddFomcAllPct\%, against \rhabLgbmFullAllPct, \rhabXgbFullAllPct{} and \rhabRfFullAllPct\% for the full set. Removed from the full set, it raises the QLIKE of LightGBM and XGBoost by \rhabLgbmLoFomcAllPct{} and \rhabXgbLoFomcAllPct\%, against \rhabLgbmLoRmAllPct{} and \rhabXgbLoRmAllPct\% for the realized moments. A share averages the forecast's movement over all bars, and the calendar moves the forecast on few bars (Section~\ref{sec:rh_fi_event}). What a series adds to accuracy is measured by the ablations. (2) In the opening bullet, replace the sentence 'How much a model uses a series is a poor guide to these gains (Section~\ref{sec:rh_fi_use}).' (it starts at the end of line 132 and ends at line 135, around the 3c6ccc4 comment lines 133-134, which stay) with: The trees' attribution understates the FOMC calendar's part in these gains (Section~\ref{sec:rh_fi_use}). Every macro is already loaded; no generator, macro or table changes.

rationale: The data settle that the general sentence is false and that the reversal belongs to the calendar, not to one pair: the calendar is out of order against four larger groups in every tree. The final text keeps the author-record lens's FOMC-versus-RM contrast as evidence (the two removals side by side), so it loses nothing the pair reading had. Tier T2: the agreement is a majority, resolved by the checked discordant-pair count and the introduction's own ordering. Confidence 0.78, not higher: the author-record lens, the lens that predicts the author, chose the pair framing, and the heading wording is a drafting choice; the author-endorsed claim 3 of 27 Oct, which is about the calendar alone, supports the final answer.
